findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed hot water tap of hand sink to be nonfunctional. Only the cold tap was working during the inspection. Ensure the hot water to the hand sink is repaired. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/31/2025 to ensure the sink is repaired.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed baffles of ice machine to have mold accumulation. Ice is considered a ready-to-eat food, and therefore is a large risk for cross-contamination. PIC was informed of accumulation. A follow-up is scheduled for 3/31/2025 to ensure ice machine is emptied and deep cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed blue cheese used for Bloody Mary cocktails to be stored portioned in a ziploc bag with no date mark. PIC was informed of proper date marking practices and the cheese was voluntarily discarded. Ensure blue cheese and milk products are date marked if kept refrigerated longer than 24 hours after opening or portioning into a new container.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed three dead roaches in the facility. Two were located behind the bar and one was located in dry storage. Debris resembling rodent dropping was also observed under the bar. PIC stated that the owner of the facility handles pest control. Hiring a professional pest control company is advised. The dry storage area had some stray pretzels on the floor near the dead insect. Ensure the facility is frequently cleaned to avoid pest accumulation. Additional pest control measurements are recommended. A spot check for improvement will be conducted on 3/31/2025 during the scheduled follow-up.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed facility to have no test strips available. Test strips were acquired during the inspection from a neighboring establishment. Ensure staff have test strips at all times and are using them to test proper sanitizer concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a few small holes next to and above the hand wash sink behind the bar. These holes can contribute to pest movement throughout the facility as well has accumulate soil and debris. Ensure walls, floors, and ceilings are smooth and easily cleanable to promote a clean space.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed interior of ice machine to be soiled with mold and debris. Remove all ice from machine, and clean and sanitize interior of ice machine. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed clean utensils stored in dirty basket at bar. Clean and sanitize basket and all utensils.

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed mop head stored head down in water filled mop bucket. Store mop in a fashion that promotes drying. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed chunks of black mold to have fallen out of the inside of the ice making section of the ice machine and into the ice in the ice bin. Empty and properly clean the ice machine so that it is not contaminating the food (ice) with mold. 
4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed cooler in small storage room next to the bar to be holding at 50F according to the internal thermometer. Two quarts of pumpkin spice flavored cream registers 45F internally. Four pints of half and half register 45F internally. Three, four ounce portions of feta cheese register 50F internally and  two, four ounce portions of blue cheese register 50F internally. These foods were discarded in the garbage. The garbage was taken out to the dumpster. Do not store food that requires refrigeration for safety in this unit until it is either repaired or replaced. Maintain time temperature control for safety foods at 41F or below. 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12  (Pf) Disposable paper towels not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide disposable paper towels at hand washing sinks. Reference 6-301.12. Paper towels were provided. Use only disposable towels for hand drying.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Open quart of cream in the facility is not marked with a use-by date. Potentially hazardous (PHF), ready to eat foods held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17. PHF foods are also known as TCS foods or Time Temperature Controlled for Safety. Cream was discarded as it had been open for more than 7 days. Smaller quantities of cream may need to be used in order to avoid waste.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination at the bar. Open bowels of pretzels are observed to be sitting on the bar upon arrival. At all times food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11. The bowls were emptied and washed. Individual portions of pretzels may be given to customers.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14. Upon arrival a wet wiping cloth was observed to be on the bar. Store wet wiping cloths properly in sanitizer between uses. A bucket of chlorine sanitizer water was provided.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Single-service articles are not protected from contamination at the bar top. Drinking straws are observed to be in holders uncovered and unprotected from coughs, sneezes and other sources of contamination. Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14. Test kit for quat sanitizer (Sani tabs) is not provided to the facility. Chlorine and chlorine test strips are available. 3 Part sink and sani bucket were made using chlorine.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: 750-280 To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used by employees or provided to consumers who serve themselves. Observed cups used to dispense pretzels stored in the bins with the pretzels. Scoops with handles were discussed with the PIC and they said that they would acquired some in the near future.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750.820e. Moist cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. Observed a cloth laying on the counter during the inspection. Discussed with the manager and the cloth was moved into a fresh solution during the inspection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use. Observed the nozzles of the 2 soda guns to be soiled during the inspection. Discussed the possible contamination of drinks that this could cause with the PIC. Nozzles were set to soak as the first part of the cleaning process during the inspection.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Chlorine test kit was not available for checking concentration of bleach solutions in sani-buckets and during ware washing at 3 part sink.
Obtain and use test strips to verify proper sanitizing concentration.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text:
750.1390 - Wet mop head was observed stored in mop bucket. Store wet mops hanging or inverted to allow for proper drying of wet mop heads.

Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored properly. 
**NOTE: Wet mop heads can serve as a food and water source for pests**
